subject: MSA + Order Form: rights matrix and legal clearance timeline
messages:
From: Diane Morris <diane.morris@novacorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Novacorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed MSA / Order Form redlines (output ownership + training)

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Attached are Novacorp's preferred redlines to the MSA and the Order Form. High level the legal team is asking us to: 1) retain ownership of product outputs that contain our confidential data, 2) prohibit training the Provider's models on Novacorp customer data without explicit opt-in, and 3) require a narrow feedback/license for quality improvements (no broader rights).

Specific asks we want you to consider:
- Replace any "assignment" language with a perpetual, non-exclusive license back to Novacorp for outputs derived from our content.
- Add a clause requiring written opt-in before any training/retraining that uses customer data.
- Limit any telemetry/feedback use to aggregated, anonymized metrics and a delete-on-demand workflow.

Attached: Novacorp_MSA_blackline_20271011.docx (redlines) and OrderForm_Novacorp_v2.pdf. Can your legal and security teams review and propose reconciliations by EOD Tuesday (10/12)? Novacorp is on a compressed procurement timeline for Q4 go-live.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Best,
Diane Morris
Sr. Counsel, Novacorp
Diane.Morris@novacorp.com

Diane — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. Looping in our legal (Laura) and product/ops (Marissa) so we can review trade-offs quickly.

Quick notes from a product/ops lens (Marissa):
- We can support making outputs explicitly available to Novacorp (export/retention controls + export logs).
- Training opt-in is feasible but has operational implications (data pipelines, isolation, and scheduler windows). We'll need ~3–4 weeks to fully isolate and validate a retrain flow if Novacorp opts in.

Laura — can you review the attached blackline and Diane's asks and propose specific language we can return by EOD tomorrow? If there are negotiation levers (e.g., telemetry limited to aggregated usage vs. per-request metadata), flag them.

Diane / procurement — can you share any internal procurement constraints or a preferred sign-off authority? That will help us target a single proposed redline.

Thanks — I'll coordinate a short review call after Laura's initial read.

Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed MSA / Order Form redlines (output ownership + training)

Karthik / Marissa / Diane —

I've reviewed Novacorp's blackline and summarized our proposed positions below. I included suggested contract snippets in the attached redwood-proposed-rights-snippet.txt for quick copy/paste.

1) Output ownership / use of outputs
- Position: Redwood proposes to grant Novacorp a perpetual, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use, reproduce, and distribute outputs that contain Novacorp's Confidential Information. We do not agree to an assignment of title.
- Rationale: assignment is a broad commercial risk; a license with explicit rights gives Novacorp the operational control they want while preserving Redwood's platform IP.

2) Training / model retraining using customer data
- Position: Redwood accepts training on customer data only with written, transactional opt-in per dataset/scope. We can add a defined "opt-in" process and a 30–90 day operational lead time (Marissa to confirm exact window).
- Rationale: protects customer sovereignty while allowing product-improvement workflows where mutually agreed.

3) Feedback / telemetry use
- Position: Redwood will accept a limited feedback license: non-exclusive, solely to improve the Service, limited to aggregated/anonymized telemetry; we will not use customer outputs to train foundation models absent explicit opt-in. We can include a delete-on-demand path for raw logs tied to identifiable records.

Open questions we need Novacorp to confirm:
- Is a license sufficient in lieu of assignment for output use cases (export, downstream productization)?
- Acceptable opt-in cadence for retraining (Marissa: propose 45 days operational lead time as a compromise).
- Any regulatory constraints (e.g., data residency) that require us to adjust retention/hosting.

If Novacorp is comfortable with the license + opt-in framework, I can prepare redlines and a short commentary mapping each Novacorp ask to our proposed language. If not, flag specific lines where Novacorp needs assignment language and we can propose a limited carveout.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Today (10/12): confirm high-level position and opt-in cadence.
- Wed (10/13): Redwood returns clean redlines + commentary.
- Thu (10/14): optional 30-minute call to resolve final items; target signature week of 10/18.

Thanks — I'm happy to jump on a call this afternoon if Diane or procurement prefer.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
laura@redwoodinference.com

Action items for Novacorp (please reply inline):

2) Confirm acceptable opt-in operational lead time for retraining (Redwood proposes 45 days).
